method: All 30 Google Chirp 3 HD personas x 52 locales (ru-RU excluded: only 8 personas) x 2 scripts (screening call; support call with clarity traps: spelled code N X 4 7 B, a 10-digit phone number read digit by digit, a date, a time, an amount, a person's name) = 3120 clips, synthesized as LINEAR16 16 kHz. Telephony copy: 300-3400 Hz band-pass, downsample to 8 kHz, 8-bit mu-law companding, decoded back to 16-bit PCM. Every clip transcribed by Google Speech-to-Text v2 chirp_2 (us-central1, default recognizer) at 16 kHz and at 8 kHz (6240 requests). Code mapping: cmn-CN->cmn-Hans-CN, yue-HK->yue-Hant-HK, ar-XA->ar-EG, ur-IN->ur-PK, nb-NO->no-NO, he-IL->iw-IL, pa-IN->pa-Guru-IN, nl-BE->nl-NL (nl-BE unsupported by chirp_2/chirp_3). Normalisation: NFKC, lowercase, any script's digits -> 0-9, numbers spelled out as words with num2words where the language is supported (phone-like runs digit by digit, so '3:30' == 'three thirty'), Serbian Cyrillic -> Latin, then punctuation, symbols and all whitespace removed. cer_* (ranking metric) = character edit distance to a leave-one-out consensus reference: the 16 kHz transcript of one of the OTHER 29 voices that is closest to all the rest (medoid). This cancels recogniser spelling conventions that hit every voice equally (English words in Latin script inside Indian-language scripts, digits vs words) and keeps what is specific to the voice. script_cer_* = CER against the written script (absolute; inflated by those conventions). digit_err_* = edit distance on the digit sequence only (support script, format-sensitive). Clips with cer > 0.10 (374) were re-transcribed with chirp_3 (location us); the better of the two readings counts (chirp2_cer_*/chirp3_cer_* keep both). Clarity score = mean over locales of (cer_16k+cer_8k)/2 + the largest excess of a locale over that locale's median voice (worst_lang). rel_pace = characters/second relative to the median voice in the same locale and script. Cross-check: en-IN and hi-IN also transcribed with Deepgram nova-3 (same consensus method); split-half rank reliability reported (screening vs support, odd vs even locales).
